request:
A world in the OUTSIDE-GATE sector, kept after original concept.

The operations this world is built from:
- Epistemic Exteriority: a universe where value comes from what cannot be reduced to the model (science fantasy and meta-reality, scarcity shift).
- Finitely Extensible: a universe where the system remains finite yet extensible (science fantasy and meta-reality, reflexivity).
- Outfinite Dimensions: a universe where any finite state can be extended by further finite dimensions (cosmos, genesis).

When we arrive: Tern reduces his capabilities to a finite set and crosses into a region from which Aster's instruments receive no response.

The central tension we want to continue: Aster could hide an undetectable observer inside him, but does not; trust becomes the only verification available

What the course asks of this world: original conflict; outfinite motif.

sourceText: The name on the threshold was OUTSIDE-GATE. Beneath it, in smaller letters, was the dedication: concept original. It was not a reproduction of a book but a world built around the question the book had made impossible to forget. Tern reduces his capabilities to a finite set and crosses into a region from which Aster's instruments receive no response. The memorial bore the name of original concept precisely to keep the genealogy of the idea visible. Aster considered it indecent for a late civilization to treat the imagination of the past as anonymous ore: authors did not own the futures, but they deserved to remain on the map as points of intellectual origin. The final period no longer studied worlds but the mechanism by which worlds had become a curriculum. The Table itself had entered the Table, and classification now had to survive criticism without turning into religion. Kesh built his classifications as instruments of falsification: a good category had to state what it did not cover, not merely what it could absorb. At the center of the conflict was Kel, an administrator chosen precisely because they were not a specialist in the phenomenon that had reorganized the world. ‘The specialists tell me what can be done,’ 347 they said. ‘I have to answer who it may be done to.’ Kesh kept the distinction in his notes. The problem closed quickly around them: Aster could hide an undetectable observer inside him, but does not; trust becomes the only verification available. There was no clean option. Every intervention shifted the cost between persons, eras, or definitions of personhood; and refusing to intervene was itself a choice made by those who could leave. Kesh opened the analytical layer of the Table for a few seconds. The active cells were Ce — Epistemic Exteriority: value comes from what cannot be reduced to the model; Fo — Finitely Extensible: the system remains finite yet extensible; Do — Outfinite Dimensions: any finite state can be extended by further finite dimensions. Course references included original conflict; outfinite motif; original concept. The rule was strict: naming a work did not substitute for an explanation. They had to identify the mechanism that could migrate into another story and the consequences that could not be copied without remainder. Tern broke the first consensus. ‘Sometimes the ethical question is whether we are entitled to know enough to optimize.’ Vela answered without raising their voice: ‘If we can save the situation only by making the world resemble us more closely, we have not demonstrated the superiority of our solution. We have demonstrated only our power.’ It was not a pedagogical quarrel. Over the last nights, the children’s differences had become incompatible political programs. 348 THE PERIODIC TABLE OF SPECULATIVE IDEAS Aster felt the Hunger precisely when an explanation closed too elegantly. A perfect theory reduced surprise, and surprise was the last symptom that something before her had not yet become part of her. The children had noticed that their disagreement calmed her more than any extravagant universe did. Vela evaluated the solution not by efficiency but by the differences it made invisible. She found one: a local minority for whom the proposed “improvement” destroyed a practice with no equivalent. Optimizing the average concealed a small and perfectly legal extinction. The night did not end in victory. The White Hunger becomes unbearable precisely because Aster does not know whether Tern exists, suffers, or triumphs. Aster recorded the decision in the world’s provenance register and, more importantly, allowed its inhabitants to contest it. For several eras she had been learning something that seems banal to lesser powers: technical reversibility is not the same as biographical reversibility. Tern no longer tried to prove the existence of the outside. It was enough that Aster could choose not to turn it immediately into an object of knowledge. From that point onward, the conflict was no longer cosmological. It was whether love can bear something it has no right to verify. For the course, Kesh also linked the night to the SCARCITY SHIFT operator. In the Table, periodicity did not mean that the same objects reappeared, but that the same operation — makes what was rare abundant, or what was abundant rare, forcing a new economy of 349 power — could recur across different families. Thus a copy of a body, a copy of a mind, a copy of a world, and a copy of a history were not the same phenomenon, but they shared a conceptual chemistry. Vela introduced the propagation test: if you remove the speculative idea and nothing in the institutions, relationships, or vocabulary has to be rewritten, the idea has remained scenery. Kesh introduced the opposite test: if the idea seems to explain every detail, you have overcompressed the world. Between the two tests lay the region in which an element became fertile without becoming superstition. Marae added the refusal test. Who can say “no,” and what happens afterward? In universes with near-divine technology, that question often separated an instrument from a regime. A power that treats refusal as a data error can be benevolent in intention and totalitarian in structure. When the threshold closed, Aster remained silent one second longer than protocol required. The children had already noticed that this was her smallest unit of fear. 350 THE PERIODIC TABLE OF SPECULATIVE IDEAS
